items.stem: Which three dimensions does the KOF index combine?
items.answer: Economic, social and political
items.markingKey: Economic, social and political. Each has de facto (flows) and de jure (policy) components.

items.stem: Explain why small, wealthy European countries score highly on the KOF index.
items.answer: Small domestic markets make them very dependent on trade; they host TNC headquarters and finance; open borders within the EU encourage migration and tourism; and they belong to many international organisations.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Small domestic markets make them very dependent on trade; they host TNC headquarters and finance; open borders within the EU encourage migration and tourism; and they belong to many international organisations. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Distinguish between de jure globalisation and de facto globalisation.
items.answer: De facto globalisation measures actual flows and interactions; de jure globalisation measures the policies and institutions that enable or restrict those flows.
items.markingKey: De facto globalisation measures actual flows and interactions; de jure globalisation measures the policies and institutions that enable or restrict those flows. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: The merchandise exports of an East African country was 146.3 US$ billion in 1990 and 276.5 US$ billion in 2010. Calculate the percentage change over the period.
items.markingKey: M1 (new − old) ÷ old × 100 = (276.5 − 146.3) ÷ 146.3 × 100; A1 +89.0% (sign or "increase/decrease" required).

items.stem: Approximate globalisation sub-index scores (0-100): Brazil - economic 54, social 64, political 88; the Netherlands - economic 92, social 90, political 92. Assuming the three dimensions are weighted equally (as in the KOF index), calculate the overall index for each country. Explain one limitation of composite globalisation indices.
items.answer: Brazil: 68.7; the Netherlands: 91.3; limitation: weights are arbitrary, national averages hide regional differences, and data on informal or illicit flows are missing.
items.markingKey: A1 68.7; A1 91.3. R1 limitation.

items.stem:
The data below were collected for a sample of countries from the World Population Data Sheet (site: urban population (%), total fertility rate).
A: 58, 3.9; B: 53, 4.2; C: 18, 6.4; D: 28, 5.8; E: 89, 1.7; F: 84, 2.2; G: 67, 2.9; H: 70, 3.0; I: 49, 4.5; J: 81, 2.3.
Calculate Spearman's rank correlation coefficient (rs = 1 − 6Σd² / (n³ − n)) and state whether the relationship is significant at the 0.05 level (one-tailed test; critical value for n = 10: 0.564). Suggest one geographical reason for the relationship and one limitation of the data.
items.answer: Σd² = 328; rs = 1 − 6×328/(10³ − 10) = -0.988; a negative correlation that is significant at the 0.05 level.
items.markingKey: M1 ranking both variables (rank 1 = highest); M1 d² summed: Σd² = 328; A1 rs = -0.988; R1 |rs| >= 0.564 so reject the null hypothesis. R1 plausible geographical explanation; R1 limitation e.g. small sample, correlation is not causation.

items.stem: Give one strength and one weakness of the claim that economic globalisation is more important than social or political globalisation.
items.answer: Economic flows are often the driving force, but the dimensions are interdependent.
items.markingKey: For: trade and FDI drive growth and jobs. Against: culture, migration and information flows shape identities. [4]: 1 mark for a valid argument for, 1 for its development; 1 mark for a valid argument against, 1 for its development; generic points without geographical context are capped at 2.

items.stem:
Study the infographic / visual stimulus described below.

Graph description: a scatter graph of KOF index (x) against GDP per capita (y) for 20 countries shows a positive relationship; Singapore and Ireland plot well above the trend line; Gulf states plot above it; Rwanda plots below.

(a) Describe the relationship shown. [4]
(b) Using the resource and your own knowledge, suggest one reason why Ireland lies above the trend line. [6]
items.answer: (a) A positive correlation: more globalised countries tend to have higher GDP per capita, with some anomalies. (b) Large FDI from US TNCs (tech and pharmaceuticals) booking profits in Ireland inflates GDP per capita.
items.markingKey: (a) A positive correlation: more globalised countries tend to have higher GDP per capita, with some anomalies. (b) Large FDI from US TNCs (tech and pharmaceuticals) booking profits in Ireland inflates GDP per capita. Credit relevant own knowledge and named examples in (b). items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "economic globalisation".
items.answer: The integration of national economies through trade, foreign direct investment and financial flows
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the integration of national economies through trade, foreign direct investment and financial flows. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Explain how the KOF index distinguishes between de facto and de jure globalisation.
items.answer: De facto measures actual flows (trade, FDI, tourism, internet bandwidth); de jure measures policies and conditions enabling flows (tariff rates, treaties, freedom to visit), so a country may be open in law but have low actual flows.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: De facto measures actual flows (trade, FDI, tourism, internet bandwidth); de jure measures policies and conditions enabling flows (tariff rates, treaties, freedom to visit), so a country may be open in law but have low actual flows. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: "Globalisation is a recent phenomenon only since the internet." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Global trade and migration have long histories (Silk Roads, colonial empires); recent decades show acceleration due to technology and liberalisation.
items.markingKey: Global trade and migration have long histories (Silk Roads, colonial empires); recent decades show acceleration due to technology and liberalisation. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Briefly describe North Korea and explain what it reveals about low global participation.
items.answer: It has very low trade, tourism and internet access because of isolationist policies and UN sanctions. Political choices and sanctions can "switch off" a country from global flows.
items.markingKey: Context (It has very low trade, tourism and internet access because of isolationist policies and UN sanctions.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Political choices and sanctions can "switch off" a country from global flows. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to low global participation.

items.stem: Evaluate the claim that the KOF Globalisation Index is the best way to measure global interactions.
items.answer: KOF is a useful comparative tool but must be complemented by local and qualitative evidence.

items.stem: The USA's military spending in 2023 was about what share of the world total?
items.answer: About 37%
items.markingKey: About 37%. SIPRI estimated about US$916 billion out of about US$2.4 trillion.

items.stem: Isabel writes: "Military strength alone makes a country a superpower." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Superpowers combine military, economic, political and cultural power; Russia has a large military but a much smaller economy than the USA or China.
items.markingKey: Superpowers combine military, economic, political and cultural power; Russia has a large military but a much smaller economy than the USA or China. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why economic power can be converted into political influence.
items.answer: Large markets, investment and loans create dependence, giving bargaining power in trade negotiations and votes in international organisations, e.g. Chinese loans and investment in Africa. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Large markets, investment and loans create dependence, giving bargaining power in trade negotiations and votes in international organisations, e.g. Chinese loans and investment in Africa. options: smart power
UN Security Council
soft power
BRICS
items.answer: soft power
items.markingKey: C. This is the definition of soft power.

items.stem: Distinguish between soft power and hard power.
items.answer: Hard power uses coercion such as military force and sanctions; soft power uses attraction such as culture, education and values to persuade others.
items.markingKey: Hard power uses coercion such as military force and sanctions; soft power uses attraction such as culture, education and values to persuade others. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain why China is considered a rising superpower.
items.answer: Second largest economy (largest by PPP), the largest exporter, BRI investments in over 140 countries, a growing navy, technology firms (Huawei, BYD), and growing influence in the UN and BRICS.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Second largest economy (largest by PPP), the largest exporter, BRI investments in over 140 countries, a growing navy, technology firms (Huawei, BYD), and growing influence in the UN and BRICS. items.stem: Suggest why South Korea's cultural exports are an example of soft power.
items.answer: K-pop, K-dramas and films such as Parasite increase global interest in Korea, boosting tourism, brand exports (Samsung, Hyundai) and positive attitudes.
items.markingKey: K-pop, K-dramas and films such as Parasite increase global interest in Korea, boosting tourism, brand exports (Samsung, Hyundai) and positive attitudes.

items.stem: "China will replace the USA as the world's dominant superpower." Discuss this statement, with reference to examples you have studied.
items.answer: A multipolar world is more likely than a simple replacement of US dominance.
items.markingKey: Indicative content - for: economy largest by PPP and growing faster; BRI and trade networks extend influence. items.stem: The five permanent members of the UN Security Council are:
options: Brazil, India, Japan, Germany and South Africa
the BRICS countries
the G7 countries
China, France, Russia, the UK and the USA
items.answer: China, France, Russia, the UK and the USA
items.markingKey: D. Each has a veto over resolutions.

items.stem: Briefly explain why reforming the UN Security Council is difficult.
items.answer: Changes require the agreement of the permanent members, each with a veto; regional rivalries (e.g. Pakistan vs India, Argentina vs Brazil) complicate choosing new members.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Changes require the agreement of the permanent members, each with a veto; regional rivalries (e.g. Pakistan vs India, Argentina vs Brazil) complicate choosing new members. items.stem: Explain the difference between the IMF and the World Bank.
items.answer: The IMF lends short-term to stabilise currencies and balance of payments; the World Bank lends long-term for development projects such as infrastructure, health and education.
items.markingKey: The IMF lends short-term to stabilise currencies and balance of payments; the World Bank lends long-term for development projects such as infrastructure, health and education. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.answer: Vietnam: 70.3; Mongolia: 60.3

items.stem: Jonas writes: "The G20 is a formal organisation with binding laws." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: It is an informal forum without a permanent secretariat or binding decisions.
items.markingKey: It is an informal forum without a permanent secretariat or binding decisions. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Outline one argument for and one argument against the view that Global governance has been effective in managing global issues.
items.answer: Effectiveness varies: strong when interests align, weak when major powers disagree.
items.markingKey: For: G20 response to 2008 crisis. Against: UNSC deadlock (Syria, Ukraine). [4]: 1 mark for a valid argument for, 1 for its development; 1 mark for a valid argument against, 1 for its development; generic points without geographical context are capped at 2.

items.stem: Define the term "International Monetary Fund (IMF)".
items.answer: A global financial institution that promotes monetary stability and lends to countries facing balance-of-payments crises, often with conditions
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: a global financial institution that promotes monetary stability and lends to countries facing balance-of-payments crises, often with conditions. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Explain the difference between the G7 and the G20.
items.answer: The G7 is a small group of advanced Western economies plus Japan; the G20 is broader, including major emerging economies and the EU and AU, and so represents more of the world economy and population.
items.markingKey: The G7 is a small group of advanced Western economies plus Japan; the G20 is broader, including major emerging economies and the EU and AU, and so represents more of the world economy and population. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Lars writes: "IMF loans have no conditions." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: IMF loans usually come with policy conditions (conditionality), such as fiscal reforms.
items.markingKey: IMF loans usually come with policy conditions (conditionality), such as fiscal reforms. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Suggest why emerging economies created the New Development Bank in 2014.
items.answer: To provide infrastructure finance without Western-dominated conditions, to reflect their growing economic weight and to reduce dependence on the IMF and World Bank.
items.markingKey: To provide infrastructure finance without Western-dominated conditions, to reflect their growing economic weight and to reduce dependence on the IMF and World Bank.

items.stem: Using the G20 response to the 2008 financial crisis as an example, explain global governance during economic crises.
items.answer: Leaders agreed a US$1.1 trillion package in London in 2009 to restore growth. Co-ordinated action between major economies stabilised the global economy.
items.markingKey: Context (Leaders agreed a US$1.1 trillion package in London in 2009 to restore growth.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. items.stem: Which of the following best describes "political globalisation"?
options: A state with dominant global influence through economic, military, political and cultural power, e.g. the USA
A forum of 19 countries plus the EU and the African Union representing about 85% of world GDP
The diffusion of government policies and participation in international organisations, embassies, treaties and UN peacekeeping
Conditions attached to IMF and World Bank loans, such as cutting public spending, privatisation and trade liberalisation

items.markingKey: C. "political globalisation" is the diffusion of government policies and participation in international organisations, embassies, treaties and UN peacekeeping.

items.stem: Briefly explain why the IMF has been criticised by many developing countries.
items.answer: Voting shares favour wealthy countries; structural adjustment conditions (spending cuts, privatisation) increased poverty and inequality in the 1980s-90s in Africa and Latin America; and Western countries traditionally choose its head.

items.stem: Explain the role of international organisations in global governance.
items.answer: Indicative content: UN and Security Council, G7/G20, IMF, World Bank, WTO; examples (Greece, 2008 crisis); influence on sovereignty; criticisms and reform.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: UN and Security Council, G7/G20, IMF, World Bank, WTO; examples (Greece, 2008 crisis); influence on sovereignty; criticisms and reform. Paper 1 extended-response markbands [10]: 9-10 responds to all demands of the question; accurate, detailed knowledge and understanding; well-developed, relevant examples and case studies with specific (named, located, quantified) detail; balanced, well-structured evaluation leading to a substantiated conclusion. 7-8 responds to most demands; mostly accurate knowledge; examples relevant but not always fully developed; evaluation present but uneven. 5-6 some demands addressed; knowledge partly accurate; examples general or loosely linked; evaluation mostly implicit. 3-4 limited, largely descriptive; little use of examples. 1-2 little relevant knowledge or understanding. 0 does not reach the standard of the descriptors.

items.stem: Examine the reasons why the KOF Globalisation Index is the best way to measure global interactions in some places but not in others.
items.answer: covers economic, social and political dimensions; long time series since 1970 allows comparison
items.markingKey: Paper 3 (a) indicative content: covers economic, social and political dimensions; long time series since 1970 allows comparison; national averages hide inequality; weightings and indicators are chosen subjectively; informal flows missed. items.stem: Explain the arguments that geographers use to support the view that China will replace the USA as the world's dominant superpower.
items.answer: economy largest by PPP and growing faster; BRI and trade networks extend influence
items.markingKey: Paper 3 (a) indicative content: economy largest by PPP and growing faster; BRI and trade networks extend influence; USA still leads in military, finance (dollar), technology and alliances; China faces an ageing population, debt and slower growth. items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The spread of ideas, information, culture and people, measured by tourism, migration, internet use and trade in cultural goods"?
options: political globalisation
globalisation
G7
social globalisation
items.answer: social globalisation
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of social globalisation.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "emerging economy"?
options: A country with rapid economic growth and increasing global influence, e.g. China, India, Brazil
A forum of 19 countries plus the EU and the African Union representing about 85% of world GDP
A grouping of major emerging economies - Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa - which expanded from 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Indonesia
The UN body responsible for peace and security, with five permanent members holding a veto (China, France, Russia, UK, USA)
items.answer: A country with rapid economic growth and increasing global influence, e.g. China, India, Brazil
items.markingKey: A. "emerging economy" is a country with rapid economic growth and increasing global influence, e.g. China, India, Brazil.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A global financial institution that promotes monetary stability and lends to countries facing balance-of-payments crises, often with conditions"?
options: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
BRICS
emerging economy
KOF Globalisation Index
items.answer: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of International Monetary Fund (IMF).

items.stem: Distinguish between de facto globalisation and de jure globalisation.
items.answer: De facto globalisation measures actual flows and interactions; de jure globalisation measures the policies and institutions that enable or restrict those flows.
items.markingKey: De facto globalisation measures actual flows and interactions; de jure globalisation measures the policies and institutions that enable or restrict those flows. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain why economic power can be converted into political influence.
items.answer: Large markets, investment and loans create dependence, giving bargaining power in trade negotiations and votes in international organisations, e.g. Chinese loans and investment in Africa.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Large markets, investment and loans create dependence, giving bargaining power in trade negotiations and votes in international organisations, e.g. Chinese loans and investment in Africa. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between the World Bank and the IMF.
items.answer: The IMF lends short-term to stabilise currencies and balance of payments; the World Bank lends long-term for development projects such as infrastructure, health and education.
items.markingKey: The IMF lends short-term to stabilise currencies and balance of payments; the World Bank lends long-term for development projects such as infrastructure, health and education. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain why some countries have low participation in global networks.
items.answer: Landlocked location, conflict or sanctions (North Korea), limited infrastructure and internet access, low incomes, political isolation and dependence on a narrow range of exports.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Landlocked location, conflict or sanctions (North Korea), limited infrastructure and internet access, low incomes, political isolation and dependence on a narrow range of exports. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between an emerging economy and a superpower.
items.answer: A superpower has dominant influence across economic, military, political and cultural spheres (USA); an emerging economy is rapidly growing in influence but does not yet have global dominance in all spheres (India, Brazil).
items.markingKey: A superpower has dominant influence across economic, military, political and cultural spheres (USA); an emerging economy is rapidly growing in influence but does not yet have global dominance in all spheres (India, Brazil). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: "IMF loans have no conditions." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: IMF loans usually come with policy conditions (conditionality), such as fiscal reforms.
items.markingKey: IMF loans usually come with policy conditions (conditionality), such as fiscal reforms. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Refer to the data below.

Table: KOF Globalisation Index 2023 edition (2021 data, approximate) - Switzerland 90.8; Netherlands 90.1; Germany 88.1; Brazil 61.6; India 62.4; Ethiopia 45.5; Eritrea 32.3.

Suggest why India and Brazil have similar scores despite different populations.
items.answer: Both are large economies with big domestic markets, so trade is a smaller share of GDP; both participate in G20 and BRICS but have lower social globalisation per person than small European states.
items.markingKey: Both are large economies with big domestic markets, so trade is a smaller share of GDP; both participate in G20 and BRICS but have lower social globalisation per person than small European states. Award 1 mark per valid point or correct step, up to [2]; data quoted must include units; points must be drawn from the resource.

items.stem: Using the Belt and Road Initiative as an example, explain economic power of an emerging superpower.
items.answer: China has financed ports, railways and power plants in over 140 countries since 2013, such as the Mombasa-Nairobi railway and Hambantota port in Sri Lanka. Infrastructure finance extends political and economic influence.
items.markingKey: Context (China has financed ports, railways and power plants in over 140 countries since 2013, such as the Mombasa-Nairobi railway and Hambantota port in Sri Lanka.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Infrastructure finance extends political and economic influence. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to economic power of an emerging superpower.

items.stem: In a recent year Germany provided about US$36.9 billion of official development assistance; its GNI was about US$4,700 billion. Calculate ODA as a percentage of GNI and compare it with the UN target of 0.7%. How much extra ODA (US$ billion) would be needed to meet the target?
items.answer: 0.79% of GNI (above 0.7%); no extra needed - target already met

items.stem: A data table shows the merchandise exports of a South Asian garment-exporting country: 1995 - 271.5 US$ billion; 2007 - 387.1 US$ billion. Calculate the percentage change over the period.
items.markingKey: M1 (new − old) ÷ old × 100 = (387.1 − 271.5) ÷ 271.5 × 100; A1 +42.6% (sign or "increase/decrease" required).

items.stem: Using named examples, compare how two countries use hard and soft power.
items.answer: e.g. USA: hard - largest military, about 750 overseas bases, sanctions, the dollar; soft - Hollywood, universities, tech brands. China: hard - navy in the South China Sea, economic leverage; soft - Confucius Institutes, BRI, TikTok, panda diplomacy.
items.markingKey: e.g. USA: hard - largest military, about 750 overseas bases, sanctions, the dollar; soft - Hollywood, universities, tech brands. China: hard - navy in the South China Sea, economic leverage; soft - Confucius Institutes, BRI, TikTok, panda diplomacy.

items.stem: In a recent year Norway provided about US$5.8 billion of official development assistance; its GNI was about US$570 billion. Calculate ODA as a percentage of GNI and compare it with the UN target of 0.7%. How much extra ODA (US$ billion) would be needed to meet the target?
items.answer: 1.02% of GNI (above 0.7%); no extra needed - target already met

items.stem: Approximate globalisation sub-index scores (0-100): India - economic 50, social 51, political 88; Germany - economic 83, social 88, political 95. Assuming the three dimensions are weighted equally (as in the KOF index), calculate the overall index for each country. Explain one limitation of composite globalisation indices.
items.answer: India: 63.0; Germany: 88.7; limitation: weights are arbitrary, national averages hide regional differences, and data on informal or illicit flows are missing.
items.markingKey: A1 63.0; A1 88.7. R1 limitation.

items.stem: Give one strength and one weakness of the claim that China will replace the USA as the world's dominant superpower.
items.answer: A multipolar world is more likely than a simple replacement of US dominance.

items.stem: "Global governance has been effective in managing global issues." To what extent do you agree with this statement? In your answer, consider the perspectives of people in high- and low-income countries.
items.answer: Effectiveness varies: strong when interests align, weak when major powers disagree.
